financials_interim.notes: Company (standalone parent-entity, holding company) basis -- no discontinued-operations split at this level, PBT/tax/PAT chain reconciles directly (1,143,616 - 80,439 = 1,063,177, matches printed exactly). EPS 0.91 = 1,063,177 / 1,165,397,072, matches printed. Company revenue is almost entirely dividend/management-fee income from subsidiaries and associates given Melstacorp is a pure holding company -- Other Operating Income of 976,081 (mostly dividend income 976,075 per the cash flow statement) dwarfs the 57,217 'Revenue' line. short_term_borrowings = bank overdrafts and other short term borrowings (4,240,536) -- no separate current interest-bearing loans line at Company level. long_term_borrowings = 0 (no non-current interest-bearing loans and borrowings at Company level; the entire non-current liabilities balance of 1,419,874 is deferred tax liabilities, retirement benefits and lease liabilities). capex = 'Acquisition of Property, Plant & Equipment, Investment Property and intangible assets' (1,944,090), Company column -- no separate intangible/investment-property lines disclosed for the Company.

Group basis. Revenue extraction note: the printed income statement line reads '6 7,472,488' -- the leading '6' is note-reference 6 merged by PDF extraction with the actual figure '67,472,488'; corrected/confirmed against the segmental note (pg.8) which independently states 'Gross revenue from continuing operations 67,472,488' and against the printed variance % (7.93% vs prior 62,514,345 -- 67,472,488/62,514,345-1 = 7.93%, matches exactly). profit_before_tax/tax_expense/profit_after_tax use the COMBINED continuing+discontinued figures (10,020,370 / 4,222,998 / 5,797,372) taken from the cash flow statement's 'Profit before tax' line (pg.7) rather than the income statement's continuing-only PBT subtotal (9,919,222) -- this is because MELS separately reports a small discontinued-operations result (Rs.101,148k PAT, no tax charge) below the continuing-operations PBT/tax/PAT block; using the combined PBT reconciles exactly to the total 'Profit for the period' (10,020,370 - 4,222,998 = 5,797,372, matching printed profit for the period to the rupee), whereas continuing-only PBT less continuing-only tax (9,919,222 - 4,222,998 = 5,696,224) does not equal profit_after_tax and would trip the identity check. operating_profit = 'Profit from Operations' (8,309,780), continuing operations only, as printed. EPS 4.61 = 5,368,877 (profit attributable to equity holders, total incl. discontinued) / 1,165,397,072 shares -- matches printed EPS and note 7 (pg.10) confirming 1,165,397,072 shares used for the EPS calculation. short_term_borrowings = interest bearing loans and borrowings, current (7,251,029) + bank overdrafts and other short term borrowings (29,552,714) = 36,803,743; long_term_borrowings = interest bearing loans and borrowings, non-current, only (39,648,163) -- lease liabilities (current 3,140,442 + non-current 31,685,183) excluded as a separately labelled line item, not bank/market debt. capex = 'Acquisition of Property, Plant & Equipment, Investment Property and intangible assets' (2,996,551) + 'Acquisition of intangible assets' (38,714) + 'Acquisition of Investment properties' (1,994,528) = 5,029,793 -- the first line's label appears to overlap with the latter two (possibly a filing labelling artifact where the first line is really just PPE), but all three are genuine capital outflows per the cash flow statement so are summed as total capex; treat the PPE/investment-property/intangible split with some caution given the ambiguous first-line label. trade_payables uses 'Trade and other payables' only (54,192,860), excluding the separate 'Other liabilities' current line (364,743).

thesis.thesis_text: Melstacorp PLC is a large, diversified Sri Lankan conglomerate anchored by a market-leading Beverages franchise, alongside Tourism, a Strategic Investment segment (telecom, insurance and other associate/JV stakes), and Financial Services. In Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), Group Revenue grew a genuine 7.9% YoY to Rs.67,472,488k, but Group operating profit fell 14.8% to Rs.8,309,780k as the Beverages segment -- ~64% of Group revenue -- absorbed a 10.5% rise in excise duty and 17.9% higher cost of sales even as its own revenue grew 13.0%, a real margin squeeze rather than a volume problem, while Tourism's PBT loss more than doubled to Rs.(1,288,100)k. Group PAT still rose 4.4% to Rs.5,797,372k, but this growth is masked-quality: it is driven almost entirely by the Strategic Investment segment's profit surging 840% to Rs.1,336,100k and a 74.3% rise in equity-accounted associate income (confirmed organic, Note 11), both less-controllable, non-core drivers. At ~10.36x annualised P/E and ~0.92x P/B, the stock is fairly valued rather than cheap once the core-operating deterioration is accounted for (Interim Financial Statements, source_doc_id manual_eddbb2a3f535db8f, segmental note p.8).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no excise-policy or Sri Lankan tourism-demand data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). Confidence is limited: only ONE interim quarter is on file (first financial_statements entry for MELS in this DB, no prior quarter for QoQ), and the filing does not name the individual entities within the Strategic Investment segment or the specific associates behind the Rs.941,900k equity-accounted income -- both genuine disclosure gaps on the items currently driving Group PAT growth.

financial_quality.rationale: Q1 FY2026/27 (qtr ended 30 June 2026) Group PAT grew 4.4% YoY to Rs.5,797,372k, but this masks a genuine operating-margin contraction: Group operating profit ('Profit from Operations') FELL 14.8% YoY to Rs.8,309,780k from Rs.9,757,312k, and operating margin fell to 12.3% from 15.6%. The balance sheet remains solid -- total liabilities/equity of 0.83x (201,223,306/241,377,863) and a current ratio of 1.30x (128,230,430/98,780,246) -- and Cash from Operating Activities was positive at Rs.5,670,075k. However, the operating-profit decline is a real, cash-flow-relevant deterioration in the core operating businesses, not merely a presentational effect, and is only offset at the PAT line by non-operating/associate income (detailed under growth_outlook).

growth_outlook.rationale: Group Revenue grew a genuine 7.9% YoY to Rs.67,472,488k, but Group PAT growth (+4.4%) is a LOWER-QUALITY outcome than the headline suggests, per the interim update's own segment bridge (Note, p.8-9): the Beverages segment (largest, ~64% of revenue) grew revenue 13.0% YoY to Rs.43,388,500k but its own segment profit FELL 7.1% to Rs.7,456,200k as excise duty rose 10.5% (Rs.28,170,400k) and cost of sales/net benefits paid rose 17.9% (Rs.22,287,100k) -- a genuine margin squeeze in the core business. Tourism's PBT loss more than doubled to Rs.(1,288,100)k from Rs.(501,800)k. The segment actually driving Group PAT growth this quarter is Strategic Investment, whose profit surged 840% YoY to Rs.1,336,100k (from Rs.142,100k), plus Share of Profit of Equity-Accounted Investees rising 74.3% to Rs.941,900k -- confirmed organic (no disposal gain this year, per Note 11, unlike the prior year's Melsta GAMA divestment) but still a less-controllable, non-core-operating driver than Beverages or Tourism performance. Treating the Strategic Investment surge as lower-quality growth, the underlying operating trajectory (core segments) is negative this quarter, not positive.

valuation.rationale: At Rs.191.00 (2026-08-31), annualising Q1 Group EPS (Rs.4.61 x4 = Rs.18.44) implies a P/E of ~10.36x, and book value of ~Rs.207.15/share (Group total equity Rs.241,377,863k / 1,165,397,072 shares) implies a P/B of ~0.92x -- reasonable rather than cheap. Dividends have been Rs.7.32 (FY2025), Rs.8.27 (FY2024), and Rs.6.76 (FY2023) -- not a clean uptrend, implying a ~3.83% trailing yield off the most recent payment. Given the genuine operating-margin compression documented under growth_outlook, the ~10.4x annualised P/E is fair rather than a bargain, since a meaningful share of this quarter's earnings came from Strategic Investment and associate income rather than the core operating businesses.
citations: dividends: FY2025 DPS 7.32, FY2024 DPS 8.27, FY2023 DPS 6.76

business_quality.rationale: Melstacorp PLC (Food, Beverage & Tobacco sector) is a large, diversified Sri Lankan conglomerate anchored by a market-leading Beverages franchise (spirits/beverages, ~64% of Group revenue), alongside Tourism, Strategic Investment (telecom, insurance and other minority holdings held via associates/JVs), and a smaller Financial Services segment. The Beverages segment's genuine 13.0% YoY revenue growth this quarter demonstrates continued franchise demand strength even as excise-driven cost pressure squeezed its margin -- a structural, ongoing risk (excise duty) rather than a one-off, common to the sector. The diversification into Strategic Investment/associate stakes provides a real, if less-controllable, additional earnings stream.

governance_risk.rationale: No circulars/disclosures feed exists to independently verify board or ownership changes. Segment disclosure (revenue and profit by segment, p.8) is reasonably transparent, a positive, but the interim filing does not name which individual entities sit within the Strategic Investment segment (the 840% profit surge driver) or which specific associates contributed the Rs.941,900k Share of Profit of Equity-Accounted Investees -- both genuine disclosure gaps on the very items now driving Group PAT growth.

key_reasons: Q1 FY2026/27 Group revenue grew a genuine 7.9% YoY to Rs.67,472,488k, but Group operating profit FELL 14.8% to Rs.8,309,780k as the Beverages segment (largest, ~64% of revenue) absorbed a 10.5% excise duty rise and 17.9% higher cost of sales even as its own revenue grew 13.0% -- a real margin squeeze in the core business, not an accounting artifact

Group PAT still grew 4.4% YoY to Rs.5,797,372k, but this growth is driven almost entirely by the Strategic Investment segment (profit +840% YoY to Rs.1,336,100k) and a 74.3% rise in equity-accounted associate income (Rs.941,900k, confirmed organic per Note 11) -- lower-quality, less-controllable drivers masking the operating-profit decline
Valuation is fair rather than cheap (~10.36x annualised P/E, ~0.92x P/B, ~3.83% yield) given the genuine core-operating deterioration sitting beneath the headline PAT growth
watch_factors: Beverages segment margin compression (segment profit -7.1% despite +13.0% revenue growth) on rising excise duty is a structural, ongoing sector risk worth monitoring for further pressure in coming quarters
Tourism segment's PBT loss more than doubled YoY to Rs.(1,288,100)k from Rs.(501,800)k -- the largest negative segment swing this quarter, compounding the Beverages margin pressure

The Strategic Investment segment's 840% profit surge and the individual associates behind the Rs.941,900k equity-accounted income are not named in the filing -- their durability cannot be independently verified, and PAT growth currently depends heavily on these items continuing

horizon_notes.6m: Next quarterly filing will show whether Beverages segment margin recovers or excise-driven compression persists, and whether the Strategic Investment segment's profit surge repeats or normalises.
horizon_notes.1y: If core operating profit (Beverages, Tourism) does not recover while Strategic Investment/associate income normalises, Group PAT growth could reverse -- worth tracking the two profit sources separately rather than the consolidated PAT figure.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends on whether Melstacorp's core Beverages franchise can pass through excise-duty increases via pricing without volume loss, and whether Tourism segment losses stabilise.
horizon_notes.5y: No macro/industry data source in this project to assess a multi-year Sri Lankan excise-policy or tourism-demand cycle relevant to MELS's two largest operating segments.

interim_updates.note_text: Melstacorp PLC (MELS) reported Group revenue of Rs.67,472.5mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026), up 7.9% YoY from Rs.62,514.3mn, but Group operating profit ('Profit from Operations') fell 14.8% YoY to Rs.8,309.8mn from Rs.9,757.3mn -- a clear margin story. By segment (pg.8 note), Beverages -- the largest segment -- grew revenue 13.0% YoY to Rs.43,388.5mn but its own segment profit fell 7.1% to Rs.7,456.2mn from Rs.8,024.6mn, squeezed between a 10.5% rise in excise duty (Rs.(28,170.4)mn vs Rs.(25,483.4)mn) and a 17.9% rise in cost of sales and net benefits paid (Rs.(22,287.1)mn vs Rs.(18,910.4)mn). Tourism was the weakest segment: revenue fell 8.9% YoY to Rs.11,529.2mn and the segment swung to a wider PBT loss of Rs.(1,288.1)mn from Rs.(501.8)mn a year earlier -- the single largest drag on segment profit this quarter. Offsetting this, the Strategic Investment segment's profit surged to Rs.1,336.1mn from Rs.142.1mn (+840%), and Share of Profit of Equity-Accounted Investees (associates/joint ventures) rose 74.3% YoY to Rs.941.9mn from Rs.540.3mn -- note 11 (pg.9) shows this is entirely organic growth in continuing JV/associate profit (no gain on disposal this year, unlike the prior year's Melsta GAMA transaction), so it reflects a genuine and growing contribution from MELS's associate stakes (telecom, insurance and other minority holdings held via the Strategic Investment segment) rather than a one-off gain. Group PAT rose 4.4% YoY to Rs.5,797.4mn from Rs.5,551.8mn -- growth driven almost entirely by the Strategic Investment segment and associate income offsetting the Beverages margin squeeze and the Tourism segment's widening loss, not by core operating momentum, which actually contracted (operating margin fell to 12.3% from 15.6%).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the first financial_statements entry for MELS in this database, so no prior quarter (e.g. Q4 FY2025/26, quarter ended 31 March 2026) is available for a sequential comparison -- only the filing's own YoY comparative column is used. Genuine disclosure gap: the Strategic Investment segment's underlying holdings (which entity/entities drove the 840% profit jump) are not named in this interim filing -- the segmental note gives only segment-level revenue and PBT, not a breakdown of what sits inside 'Strategic Investment', so the specific driver behind that swing cannot be identified from this filing alone. Similarly, the associate/JV note (11) does not name which individual associates contributed the Rs.941.9mn share of profit.
interim_updates.takeaway: MELS's headline PAT growth (+4.4% YoY) masks a genuine operating-margin contraction: core operating profit fell 14.8% as Beverages -- the biggest segment -- absorbed a 10.5% excise duty increase and 17.9% higher cost of sales even as its revenue grew, and Tourism's PBT loss more than doubled to Rs.(1,288.1)mn. The segment actually driving profit growth this quarter is Strategic Investment (+840% to Rs.1,336.1mn) together with a 74.3% rise in equity-accounted associate income (Rs.941.9mn) -- both largely outside the operating businesses' direct control, meaning the quality of this quarter's earnings growth is weaker than the headline PAT number suggests.
operational_highlights: Group revenue up 7.9% YoY to Rs.67,472.5mn (from Rs.62,514.3mn); Group operating profit fell 14.8% YoY to Rs.8,309.8mn (from Rs.9,757.3mn) -- a clear margin contraction despite top-line growth

Beverages segment (largest, ~64% of revenue): revenue +13.0% YoY to Rs.43,388.5mn, but segment profit -7.1% to Rs.7,456.2mn as excise duty rose 10.5% to Rs.(28,170.4)mn and cost of sales/net benefits paid rose 17.9% to Rs.(22,287.1)mn -- a margin squeeze, not a volume problem
Tourism segment: revenue -8.9% YoY to Rs.11,529.2mn; segment PBT loss widened to Rs.(1,288.1)mn from Rs.(501.8)mn -- the single largest negative swing among all segments this quarter
Strategic Investment segment profit surged to Rs.1,336.1mn from Rs.142.1mn (+840% YoY) -- the largest single driver of Group profit growth this quarter

Share of Profit of Equity-Accounted Investees (associates/JVs) up 74.3% YoY to Rs.941.9mn from Rs.540.3mn; note 11 (pg.9) confirms this is organic growth in continuing associate profit, with no disposal gain this year (unlike FY2025/26's Melsta GAMA divestment)
Financial Services segment swung to a small loss of Rs.(46.1)mn from a Rs.108.2mn profit a year earlier
Group PAT +4.4% YoY to Rs.5,797.4mn (Rs.5,551.8mn); EPS +2.5% to Rs.4.61 (Rs.4.49) -- growth driven by Strategic Investment and associate income, not core operating segments
key_drivers: Beverages segment margin compression: revenue grew 13.0% YoY (Rs.43,388.5mn) but segment profit fell 7.1% to Rs.7,456.2mn as excise duty (+10.5% to Rs.28,170.4mn) and cost of sales/net benefits paid (+17.9% to Rs.22,287.1mn) outgrew revenue -- the single biggest drag on Group operating profit
Tourism segment PBT loss more than doubled YoY to Rs.(1,288.1)mn from Rs.(501.8)mn on an 8.9% revenue decline to Rs.11,529.2mn -- the largest negative swing of any segment

Strategic Investment segment profit up 840% YoY to Rs.1,336.1mn (from Rs.142.1mn), combined with a 74.3% rise in share of profit from equity-accounted associates/JVs (Rs.941.9mn vs Rs.540.3mn, confirmed organic per note 11) -- together these more than offset the Beverages and Tourism weakness and are the reason Group PAT still grew 4.4% YoY despite the 14.8% fall in core operating profit
